name: [Portal] Reviews & ratings data model (DB)
description:
### Summary

`partners_web`'s contract (`contract/openapi.yaml`) requires `averageRating`, `reviewCount`, `ratingStars` (per-star histogram) and a full `reviews` thread (with partner replies) on every professional, plus a form endpoint (`POST /professionals/{slug}/reviews`) that accepts a review or a reply to one, confirmed by e-mail (double opt-in) before publication. No table in `st_crm` holds reviews today — CZ3TDR1-572 only covers the partner and category records themselves.

### Why?

Without a reviews table, `averageRating`/`reviewCount`/the reviews list can never be real data — they would have to be faked or omitted, which breaks the partner profile page and the professionals-listing sort order (verified level → review count → rating → title).

### What?

A `partner_review` table able to represent both a visitor review and a partner's reply to it (self-referencing `parentId`), carrying the double-opt-in/moderation lifecycle, a nullable `rating` (null for replies), and an author e-mail that is stored for the confirmation flow but never selected by any read path — the same "never returned" rule already applied to `partner_lng`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `partner_review` table created via a migration under `migrations/2026/devrel/crm/CZ3TDR1-673/`, following the `_drop.sql` stage and `ALGORITHM=`/`LOCK=` rules in `migrations/AGENTS.md`
- [ ] Columns: `id`, `partnerId` (FK → `partner.id`), `parentId` (nullable, self-FK, covers partner replies and threaded replies), `rating` (nullable, 1-5), `content` (text), `authorName`, `authorEmail` (never selected by any read query), `authorUrl` (nullable), `status` (draft / pendingConfirmation / approved / rejected), `confirmationToken`, `isPartnerReply` (bool), `createdAt`, `approvedAt`
- [ ] Composite index supporting "approved top-level reviews per partner" aggregate queries (`partnerId`, `status`, `parentId`)
- [ ] `make lint-migrations` passes

### Open questions

- Is an expired/rejected confirmation token cleaned up, or kept for audit? (proposed: keep — cheap, useful for abuse investigation)

### Resources

- Epic: CZ3TDR1-614
- Depends on: CZ3TDR1-572 (`partner` table)
- Feeds: the reviews domain-layer task filed alongside this one

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Sonnet 5, 2026-09-22, from a review of _`partners_web/contract/openapi.yaml` (`Review`, `RatingHistogram`, `ReviewBody` schemas) against `database/schema/st_crm.sql`, which currently has no review table.
